about: The 100 features of master command v2 plus 101-103 from plan/women-first-brief.md. Hand-written facts only: what exists, where it lives, which plan round has it, or why it is blocked. Scores are never written here; registry.py reads them from arena results files, and a feature with no results shows Not tested. Status is Built or Blocked with an explicit reason; implementation blockers are distinguished from rights and scope blockers; Passed and Failed come only from the gates.

plan_states.new_round: needs a new round (no plan row yet)

plan.note: Try one saved look on 2 to 12 photos of the same day, side by side. Every step runs through the single-photo re-apply path, each photo on its own face points read on this device (never another photo's); a photo without points still gets the steps that need no face and says what was left out. The board shows, step by step, on how many photos it ran, so an uneven trial is visible. Provider makeup and hair steps are never sent from here; each photo points to the styling screen, where a photo goes only with her consent. Gowns and robes are outfits and stay blocked.

Her own design only (the app ships none, and she confirms the art is hers to use), placed by zone, size and turn on a frontal reference face and mapped triangle by triangle onto her face mesh, so it follows the shape and turn of her face. Ink is a multiply blend, so skin texture shows through, kept inside visible skin and never over eyes, brows or lips; triangles that turn away from the camera are left uninked, judged against her mesh's own orientation so mirrored selfies work. Art without transparency has its near-white background keyed out (ASSUMED threshold). Face placement only: arms and body need a body mesh, not built. Saved with the Simulation label and no metadata.

Her edited photo cut out, outlined in white and captioned in the device's own font (no font file), as a still sticker and three one-second loops (bounce, wiggle, pulse) in one zip of PNG and animated PNG files with transparency and no metadata chunk. The cut-out uses the first real mask that exists: the on-device person segmentation when that model is enabled, else the person area she marked, else her face outline from the face points (the sticker says face only); with none it refuses. A cleaner edge waits for background removal (feature 58, not built). The caption line notes Simulation when an edit is one and her Trust Centre switch is on.

Apply a look's photo-wide edits (Enhance, Filters, Lighting) to up to 100 photos, one original decoded and rendered at a time, each at its own size, with per-photo strength, face review and redo. Past 50 photos the review thumbnails halve; when the encoded results would pass the 100 MB in-memory limit, the finished photos download as a numbered album part (Good Lookin part 1.zip, part 2 ...) and the batch keeps going. Edits that need a photo's own face points stay in the editor, and the batch says which were left out.
My Look save, apply in one tap, export and import as a file, this round. Project files come in R31.

A 4-second clip made on the device: her photo holds, a divider wipes across uncovering the edit, the edit holds. Frames are composed from the two images and recorded by the browser's own MediaRecorder through the clip job (memory limit, cancel, tracks released); MP4 where the browser records it, else WebM. The edit carries the Simulation label per her Trust Centre switch, system fonts only, nothing uploaded. A browser that can't record a canvas is told so and offered the compare image. Tested with a stand-in recorder in Node; recording in a real browser is not yet measured.

One tap per size: square post, portrait post, story, wide, long edge 1600 or as edited. The photo is cropped to the shape, never squashed; the crop keeps her whole face when the photo has face points and refuses a size that would cut it. The editor works on a device-sized copy, so enlargement stops at 2x and the file says its real size (HD export is the path for a full 1080 frame). No watermark for anyone, free or paid; only the Simulation label, which follows her Trust Centre switch. Metadata is stripped.
On-device only switch refuses every provider request (R9); now up front in the Trust Centre.

Per-face edits in a group photo of 2 to 6 faces: the hero screen hands every found face to the editor, the face chips keep each face's own edits, All copies one face's edits to every face, and the Group photo panel saves the combined photo. Each face's edits stay inside its face oval and faces without edits keep their exact pixels, checked by the person audit. Face points come from the on-device face model when it is enabled or from a matching recorded fixture. Per-person presets come in R38.

Rank 2 to 12 photos by the photo pre-check (sharpness, light, framing and the rest) plus eyes open from the lid landmarks, with a plain reason for each place; open the chosen photo in the editor. Photo quality only: no looks score and no identity check. Without face points eyes and framing are not checked and the result says so.

Local live mirror on the Video and live screen, local effects only (no provider call): the camera opens only after she ticks a camera agreement and taps start; each frame gets the chosen effect (skin smoothing, background change, enhance or a live filter) with the newest on-device face points or person outline, at most one measurement in flight so the picture never waits, and is shown mirrored. Only the current frame is held; nothing is recorded or uploaded, and one frame is saved only when she taps save. Stop, withdrawing the agreement or leaving the screen ends every camera track. Tested with a fake camera serving drawn frames; real-camera speed and quality remain unproven.

features.name: Voice-guided selfie framing for low-vision users

plan.note: Spoken cues from the 478 face points of each front-camera frame, one at a time: come closer or move back, move left or right (from her own point of view, worked out in camera-image coordinates), raise or lower the camera, level your head, face the camera, then hold still and Ready once the framing has held for a second. Cues are spoken by the browser's own speech, never faster than every 1.5 s and repeated only after 4 s; every cue also goes to a live text line for screen readers, which is all that runs where speech is missing. Use this photo opens the frame in the editor with its own points. Needs the on-device face model, still licence pending, and says so instead of starting the camera. Targets ASSUMED until tested with low-vision users; tested here with drawn points and stand-in camera and speech.

features.name: Web and desktop editor synced with mobile

plan.note: One web editor for phone and desktop (R8-R9, layout v1 this round). Sync is local project files (R31); cloud sync is post-launch.

CIEDE2000 shade matching exists; undertone classes and routing every makeup and skin feature through it in R11-R12. A local Foundation step applies the matched shade (or its runner-up) to her skin's low frequencies only, on the Shade screen: never lighter (L* only falls, byte guard), marks kept, lighter or far shades refused with codes. Coverage ASSUMED; our own reference shades, not tested against real products.

Named Grey Transition mode, designed for women 40-60; no age is asked, read or inferred. Three local decision previews in the hair she marks, each with a plain upkeep label: Cover (greys in her natural shade, regular root touch-ups), Blend (part of the silver kept as soft highlights) and Go silver (her pigmented strands in her own measured grey, as after a full grow-out). Replaces the planned YouCam blending route. Editor Grey Transition layer; TypeScript matches Python within one byte. Shares ASSUMED; a decision aid, not a salon result.
One screen: on-device mode, never-train promise, neutral defaults, simulation label, deletion with a receipt. Items not built yet say Not built.

Drawn, seeded freckles over the nose bridge and upper cheeks, placed in the face's own frame; strength sets depth, density sets count. Only darkens and warms; her own freckles and moles are untouched. Real-face quality not yet measured.

Takes down the smooth bright bump of a shine spot above the skin's broad shading and gives back the washed-out colour; fine texture is left alone and no pixel gets lighter. Real-face quality not yet measured.
Named skin glows: lifts the light the face already catches with a sheen on the high points, balanced so the average skin lightness does not rise. Real-face quality not yet measured.

Thirteen one-tap looks named after French places, one with procedural sparkle for evening. Each joins texture-kept skin polish (#25's texture graft, marks held), gentle definition on eyes, brows and lips, and a colour grade from the filter engine with the skin guard on, under one 0-100 slider; 0 changes nothing. Identity guard keeps marks and eye colour and refuses any look that would lighten skin. Python and browser give the same bytes. Real-face quality not yet measured.

plan.note: Home shows the next occasions she follows from the local seasonal calendar (Python dates, generated for the browser and checked), secular days by default and cultural or religious ones only when she ticks them, each with her own saved look kept for that day or an existing built look that opens in the studio. The Season Book asks its reviewed source again on its four edition dates. A saved recipe re-applies to a new photo through the studio's own local renderers; saved face points are reused only on the photo they came from. Nothing is sent and nothing polls.
